gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a yearly electricity cost for any cooler. ENERGY STAR rates Bob Vila's best overall, the Brio 520, and the Brio Moderna 720/730 at 0.76 kWh/day, which is about 277 kWh or $50 a year at the August 2026 US average of 18.16¢/kWh. ChatGPT's value pick, the Avalon A4, is not in ENERGY STAR's water cooler list and has no published kWh figure.
standout_why: I opened four rival pages. Bob Vila (the only page ChatGPT cited) gives only 'Energy Star-certified coolers use 30 percent less energy', a 5-minute heat-up for the A4 and a 39–194°F range for the Moderna, with no kWh or dollar figure. mybest (us.my-best.com/21237) only says 'look for Energy Star' and 'turn them off to save energy'. InspectandTest gives the A4's 420 W heating and 100 W cooling ratings and a flow rate for the Brio 130, but no kWh/day, no yearly cost and no hourly hot-water output, and it says the Brio 520 has no published power draw. Popular Mechanics would not load (fetch blocked). None of them uses the ENERGY STAR kWh/day or hot-water capacity data, and none prices a year of electricity.
decides: This backs the Brio 520 as best overall: about $50 a year, plus a rated 46 six-oz cups of hot water per hour against 8 for the low-capacity Brio 130 and 425. It weakens the Avalon A4 as the value pick. The Avalon has no ENERGY STAR listing, and on Target the listing says 'Energy Star Certified' while a brand Q&A answer says it is not. Target also sells the ENERGY STAR-certified Brio 430 (CLBL430SC, 0.79 kWh/day, about $52 a year) for $174.99, $5 under the A4's $179.99. For a light user the Brio 130 is the lowest-energy bottom-loader: 0.60 kWh/day, about $40 a year.
